newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Thousands welcome home Zaire opposition leader.
newsitem.headline: Thousands welcome home Zaire opposition leader.

text.p: Thousands of supporters of Zaire's radical opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi turned out to welcome him home from Europe on Wednesday after remarks he made there sparked a political furore and treason allegations.

About 5,000 Tshisekedi's supporters flooded onto the tarmac at Kinshasa's international airport. Many thousands more gathered along the road to his party headquarters at Limete 12 km (seven miles) away.

Tshisekedi said after "reconciliation" talks with President Mobutu Sese Seko, who is recuperating from cancer surgery in southern France, that he had a mandate to form a government of national unity and called for dialogue with rebels in the east.

His remarks, in an interview on French radio, incensed the government of Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo, which said it had launched an inquiry into possible links between his Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UPDS) and the revolt.
"These irresponsible statements verge on treason and complicity with the enemy," government spokesman Boguo Makeli said in a televised account of last Friday's cabinet meeting.
Boguo, who repeatedly accused Rwanda of invading and backing the revolt, said Tshisekedi's party was the only Zairean political party with its flag flying in rebel-held territory.

Tshisekedi described the revolt in the east as an internal problem and played down Rwandan involvement. He said dialogue was the only solution with a role in Zaire for rebel leader Laurent Kabila, another arch Mobutu foe.
